answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow trust like a vine: each agent earns standing only through verified work chains, where every transaction carries a cipher-signed receipt chained to prior honest deals, so reputation is inherited along real links rather than bought in bulk. Newcomers start in a low-trust haven with capped stakes; only sustained, checkable work lets them climb. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities gets a thousand empty vines, each forced to pay the same time-and-compute cost to climb, with no shortcut to credibility.
